assumptions: Scenario model, not a prediction: schedules the simulated transmission damage (best-track run, 10000 simulations: expected failed structures and tree-struck spans, the same damage as Team up) with a greedy list scheduler.

Crews: DESC 40, GPC 200 transmission crews = public Helene storm workforce (DESC more than 4,000 crew members, Dominion Energy 2024-10-09; GPC 20,000+ personnel, Georgia Power) x 5% assumed on transmission / 5 people per crew. The same crews are used for every storm.
Repair time: 12 crew-hours per failed pole structure, 48 per failed lattice tower, 6 per span hit by a tree (assumed).
Hour 0 = restoration start after the storm passes; mobilization, damage assessment, tree clearing and distribution work are not modeled.
Travel: OSRM drive time from the staging yard to the work, driven there and back for every job (straight line x 1.3 at 50 km/h if no route).
Separate: each utility repairs only its own assets and stages only at the nearest city/town on its own side (DESC in SC, GPC in GA).

Coordinated: shared staging at every own-side town and the joint yards in yards.json (0 for this storm), and mutual aid: a free crew takes the next job from either utility, at 85% productivity on the other utility's assets (assumed).
Both scenarios use the same priority order (electricity-dependent residents per crew-hour, then size), so savings come only from staging and mutual aid.
Work covers DESC/GPC line sections at least 1% likely to be damaged; other owners' lines are excluded. Percent restored counts expected damaged line sections (wind or trees).
Work items: 172; expected damaged line sections DESC 91.5, GPC 31.1 (7.2 failed structures and 127.5 tree-struck spans).
Shared staging alone (no mutual aid) reaches 90 % at 21.6 h and 100 % at 23.0 h, vs 30.4 h and 33.0 h separate.
